doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Teaching himself clarinet and playing in town
summary: He taught himself clarinet with his mother's help on notation and played marches for neighborhood kids.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I can’t remember if I asked you this yesterday. Coming up as a kid in Badin, did you have any instructors other than your mother? You taught yourself, I guess you said.
Yes, I taught myself. And my mother...
Your mother could help you a little bit.
With the music and the notes. Keys. Signatures on the music and all that. She didn’t know much about the clarinet, but I just read the book and found out about that.
And you figured out the embouchure and all the details...
Oh, yes. I figured all that out.
Did you perform at all before you went to Greensboro?
Oh yeah, I’d play at home, and I’d play down... I’d go down in the middle of town

and play like marches and things that I’d learned. All the kids would come around, because I was the only one playing music in the town. They’d come out, and they would listen to me. I used to tell them, “One day you’re going to have to pay to see me play.” And now, every time one of them comes to see me play, I act like I don’t know ‘em. [LAUGHS]
